note: original_verdict: SUSPICION, expected_confidence: 0.75. Delta of 10 reflects minimal artifact content. This case contrasts with FP-CULTURAL-CLEAN: here the Russian cultural markers ARE accompanied by technical corroboration (connections to RU infrastructure, execution traces). This is a true positive — the technical evidence supports the cultural attribution, unlike the false positive cases where cultural markers appear on a clean system.

peircean_analysis.firstness: Three artifacts: ART-001 — Russian-language comments in a script (source: script). ART-002 — connections to Russian infrastructure (source: network). ART-003 — valid execution traces (source: binary).
peircean_analysis.secondness: Unlike FP-CULTURAL-CLEAN (cultural markers on a technically clean system), here the Russian cultural markers are accompanied by two independent technical corroborations: (A) network connections to Russian infrastructure, (B) execution traces from a binary. The distinction from false positive cases is the combination: cultural markers alone are insufficient for SUSPICION; cultural markers plus technical activity pointing in the same direction constitute a corroborated pattern.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: Russian-language script with connections to Russian infrastructure and execution traces suggests a Russian-origin tool or actor with active operation on the target system. The presence of 'valid execution traces' implies the binary executed — not merely was present. However, 'connections to RU infra' is ambiguous (legitimate Russian CDN vs C2 infrastructure), and 'valid execution traces' does not confirm what the execution did. SUSPICION is epistemically correct — corroborated cultural + technical pattern without confirmed malicious action.

hypotheses.H1_russian_origin_activity: A Russian-origin tool or actor executed scripts on the target system and connected to Russian infrastructure. The cultural markers (comments) are authentic and corroborated by network and execution evidence.
hypotheses.H2_legitimate_russian_developer_tool: A legitimate tool written by a Russian developer (with Russian comments) is connecting to a Russian CDN or update server. Execution traces are normal tool operation.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H2: Many open-source tools are developed by Russian speakers and connect to Russian infrastructure for legitimate purposes (CDN, update servers, package repositories). Russian comments in source code are common and not inherently suspicious.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H2 NOT REFUTED — the artifact descriptions are too brief to distinguish between a malicious Russian tool and a legitimate Russian-developed tool. H2 requires additional analysis (binary content, C2 vs CDN classification of the RU infra IPs).
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H2 not refuted. SUSPICION is the honest bounded verdict.

devil_advocate: Russian-language scripts are written daily by millions of legitimate developers worldwide. Russian infrastructure hosts thousands of legitimate services. Without knowing what the binary executed or what the Russian infrastructure IPs are, the cultural + technical corroboration is suspicious but not determinative.
caie_fracture: None formally identified. Cultural corroboration pattern (cultural markers + network + execution) distinguishes this from false positive cases.
evidence_anchors: ART-001: Russian-language comments in script (cultural marker + technical artifact)
ART-002: Connections to Russian infrastructure (network corroboration)
ART-003: Valid execution traces (binary execution confirmed)
known_limitations: Minimal artifact content. RU infrastructure IPs not identified (CDN vs C2 unknown). Binary content not analyzed. Execution purpose unknown. These gaps are required to elevate beyond SUSPICION.
